curvature_speed_plan — DRIVE lateral op

• Data kinds: any → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.curvature_speed_plan(s, kappa, *, v_max, a_lat_max: 'float', a_accel: 'float', a_decel: 'float', a_total: 'Optional[float]' = None, v_start: 'Optional[float]' = None, v_end: 'Optional[float]' = None) -> 'Dict[str, np.ndarray]' (to call the implementation directly, import drivelateral; drivelateral.curvature_speed_plan(s, kappa, *, v_max, a_lat_max: 'float', a_accel: 'float', a_decel: 'float', a_total: 'Optional[float]' = None, v_start: 'Optional[float]' = None, v_end: 'Optional[float]' = None) -> 'Dict[str, np.ndarray]'; from the registry, opsdrive.get("curvature_speed_plan"))

• GPU: none (CPU reference implementation only)

Usage

Speed planning that builds a speed limit from a curvature sequence and enforces acceleration/deceleration limits with 2 passes, forward and backward (a classical method).

s: arc length (increasing, (N,)). kappa: curvature at each point (sign does not matter). v_max: speed upper limit (scalar or (N,); legal speed, crawling sections, etc.). Limit v_lim = min(v_max, √(a_lat_max/|κ|)). Between steps v² is linear in s (constant acceleration/deceleration). If a_total (radius of the friction circle, e.g. μg) is given, the longitudinal acceleration/deceleration is also bounded by √(a_total² − (v²κ_m)²) (κ_m = the larger |κ| at the two ends of the step; solved as a quadratic, so √(a_x² + a_y²) ≤ a_total anywhere within the step). Requires a_lat_max ≤ a_total. Return value: v, v_limit, ax (per-step longitudinal acceleration, (N−1,)), ay_max (maximum lateral acceleration within each step), time (arrival time, exact time for v² linear).

Raises ValueError: wrong shape, s not increasing, limit not positive, a_lat_max > a_total, v_start/v_end above the limit.
